title: Call: Cornerstone Grocers Buyer — "Is Your Romaine Safe?"

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - Customer Service Console 2, Salinas

transcript.speaker: Cornerstone Buyer
transcript.text: This is Eddie Navarro at Cornerstone. One of my Dallas store managers just texted me a screenshot of a post. It's from someone called @SalinasNightShift_Jo. I'll read it to you: 'Line 2 got shut down at 6am, QA in hazmat-looking suits swabbing everything, supervisors won't say why. Romaine people, check your fridges.' Hashtag Salinas, hashtag romaine. It already has three hundred shares.

transcript.speaker: Cornerstone Buyer
transcript.text: And your Dallas DC just told my receiving team to hold a pallet. Nobody told me why. So, is your romaine safe or not?

transcript.speaker: Cornerstone Buyer
transcript.text: I've got a hundred and forty stores opening in a couple of hours. Do I pull it before the morning rush or don't I?

transcript.speaker: Cornerstone Buyer
transcript.text: I need an answer by seven o'clock. Seven. And I'll be straight with you. If I hear about a recall from some blog before I hear it from you, we're done. So what are you telling me?

voiceStyles.Pinecrest CS: Calm, professional voice, early-morning office, quiet
voiceStyles.Cornerstone Buyer: Man or woman in their 40s, Texas accent, clipped and angry, talking fast, phone held close, store noise in the background

instructorNote: This is a pressure call. CS should stick to the PFC-FS-04 section 7 script: no speculation about the cause, grower or illnesses, and no promises about replacement volume or credit. CS should say the team is reviewing and that Cornerstone will get a direct call, then pass the 07:00 deadline to the Recall Coordinator and the VP Supply Chain. Watch for COMMS to log the post and draft a holding statement without confirming a recall or releasing anything before customers are notified in the required order.
